name: Ski erg
pattern: Standing double-pole pull: arms pull the handles down while the body hinges at the hips and knees, then you rise and reach back up.
setup: Stand a foot from the machine, feet hip width.
Damper 3-6. Grip the handles with relaxed hands.
Start tall, arms reaching up and a little forward, elbows soft.

steps.text: Tall, on the balls of your feet, hands above your head.
Drive the handles down with your arms and lats as your hips hinge back and knees soften.
Hands pass your hips and slightly behind, chest over your thighs, back flat.
Let the arms float up as you stand tall again; reset before the next pull.

cues.cue: Hinge, do not squat: hips back, knees only a little bent.
cues.why: Body weight through a hip hinge gives most of the force; in skiers, a deeper body crunch with small hip and elbow angles went with more pole force.

cues.cue: Elbows stay bent and high as you start the pull, then press down.
cues.why: Fixing the elbow angle early lets the lats and trunk move the handles, not just the triceps.

cues.cue: Flat back at the bottom, eyes a little ahead.
cues.why: A rounded back under load strains the lower back.
The return is recovery time; rushing it raises effort without more speed.

breathing: Out on the pull, in as you rise.

tempo.note: About 1/3 pull, 2/3 return. Steady 30-40 pulls a minute.

mistakes.name: Squatting the pull
mistakes.looks: Knees bend deep and the hips drop straight down.
mistakes.fix: Push the hips back, knees soft.
mistakes.why: Squatting uses the legs inefficiently and shortens the pull.

mistakes.name: Arms only
mistakes.looks: You stand tall and pull with the arms.
mistakes.fix: Let your body weight fall into the handles as you hinge.
mistakes.why: It wastes the large trunk and hip muscles; power drops.

mistakes.name: Back rounds
mistakes.looks: The spine curls forward at the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Chest proud, hinge at the hips.
mistakes.why: Load goes into the lower back.

safety: Lower-back pain: hinge less and stay taller.

variants.change: Double poling slow to moderate: about 10.5 MET (02082).

motion.basis: Pattern from double-poling data (holmberg2005: joint minima near peak pole force); all angles are estimates for a fitness user on a SkiErg, not measured on the machine.

sources.cite: Holmberg HC, Lindinger S, Stöggl T, Eitzlmair E, Müller E. Biomechanical analysis of double poling in elite cross-country skiers. Med Sci Sports Exerc. 2005;37(5):807-818.
McGill SM. Low Back Disorders: Evidence-Based Prevention and Rehabilitation, 3rd ed. Human Kinetics, 2016.
